definition: To establish, prove, or strengthen an assertion by providing concrete empirical evidence.
etymology: From Late Latin substantiātus, past participle of substantiāre.
manuscriptExample: Complementary in vivo CRISPR knockout models were deployed to substantiate observed transcriptomic downregulation.
conferenceExample: While the hypothesis is compelling, we requested the authors perform an orthogonal assay to substantiate their claim.

definition: Most prominent, conspicuous, or crucial for understanding a dataset or scientific hypothesis.
etymology: From Latin saliens, present participle of salīre ('to leap').
manuscriptExample: The most salient feature of the single-cell trajectory is the abrupt bifurcation at day 4 of stem cell differentiation.
conferenceExample: In the executive summary for the editor-in-chief, we highlighted three salient findings supporting publication.

definition: False, misleading, or apparent correlations resulting from confounding variables or experimental artifacts.
manuscriptExample: Inclusion of isotype controls prevented spurious antibody binding in immunohistochemical staining of tumor sections.
conferenceExample: The editor warned that without Bonferroni correction, the apparent correlation was likely a spurious false positive.

definition: The categorization of patient cohorts or biological samples into distinct sub-groups based on biomarker expression.
manuscriptExample: Biomarker-guided patient stratification significantly enhanced overall survival benefit in the phase III trial.
conferenceExample: Reviewer 2 recommended clinical risk stratification prior to secondary endpoint statistical analysis.

definition: An interaction where the combined efficacy of two biological agents exceeds the sum of their individual effects.
manuscriptExample: Combination treatment demonstrated potent synergy, yielding a combination index (CI) value well below 0.5.
conferenceExample: The panel queried whether the observed tumor regression reflected true drug synergy or additive cytotoxicity.
